# Discovery and Risk Map

Boruch Hashem. Blessed is He.

The Awtsmoos is not revealed through assumption but through evidence; this map names the remaining shadows so Awtsmoos.com can become searchable without sacrificing truth or privacy.

## Known evidence from prior pass

- Numeric Road URLs historically returned a loading shell before JavaScript.
- The public series details API contains ordered post IDs.
- The series-scoped singular post API returns full public Torah content.
- The old root-level singular post API is not a valid production route.
- Production previously returned 404 for robots.txt and common sitemap paths.
- Existing long-lived local servers had stale module state during the earlier pass.

## Current unknowns to resolve

- Whether current HEAD already contains the entire SEO pass.
- Whether any new commits changed route/API contracts after the earlier pass.
- Whether current long-lived processes have reloaded the SEO modules.
- Exact local server port/configuration for an isolated fresh verification process.
- Whether the dynamic response router supports a root robots endpoint cleanly or a static file is preferable.
- Whether Heichel discovery returns enough public entities for a live sitemap without expensive recursion.
- Whether direct `/post/:post` should remain indexable, redirect, or noindex when root-series lookup fails.
- Whether initial-content rendering escapes or preserves rich Torah markup safely.

## Failure risks

- Duplicate canonical identities between numeric Road and named post URLs.
- 200 loading shells for missing posts.
- Canonical URLs pointing to non-resolving paths.
- Sitemap inclusion of drafts/private/editor routes.
- Runtime fetch recursion against the same local server.
- Slow server rendering caused by many serial discovery requests.
- Broken client initialization when the post is already present in HTML.
- Stale process verification falsely representing current source.
